learn.title: Resizing and balance
learn.body: A dilation resizes a figure from a centre point, using a scale factor $k$. Unlike the moves in the last lesson, it changes size, but the image is similar to the original. We also look at symmetry, where a figure matches itself after a move.

learn.title: Dilation from the origin
learn.body: With the centre at the origin, $(x,y)\to(kx,ky)$. If $k$ is more than 1 the figure grows, and if $k$ is between 0 and 1 it shrinks. Lengths scale by $k$ and area by $k^2$. Angles stay the same.

learn.title: Line and rotational symmetry
learn.body: A figure has line symmetry if a mirror line splits it into two matching halves. It has rotational symmetry if a turn of less than $360^\circ$ makes it look the same. A square has 4 lines of symmetry and looks the same after each $90^\circ$ turn.

learn.title: Dilations
steps: Its area was $4$ and is now $1$, which is $\left(\frac12\right)^2$ of it.

learn.body: Lines of symmetry: equilateral triangle 3, rectangle that is not a square 2, regular hexagon 6, circle infinitely many.

questions.prompt: Dilate $(2,3)$ from the origin with scale factor 3.
Dilate $(8,4)$ from the origin with $k=\frac12$. What is the new $x$-coordinate?
A dilation has scale factor 3. How does the area change?
How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.explanation: Two through opposite corners and two through midpoints of opposite sides.

questions.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
questions.explanation: One through each vertex and the midpoint of the opposite side.
The shape is the same but the size changes, which is similarity.

questions.prompt: Match each figure to its lines of symmetry.
questions.explanation: A regular $n$-sided polygon has $n$ lines of symmetry. A rectangle has two.
